source.text: Καὶ ἐμβὰς εἰς πλοῖον διεπέρασεν καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν ἰδίαν πόλιν.

records.literal_gloss: And having got into a boat he crossed over and came into the own town.

en.L: And getting into a boat, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} crossed over and came to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own town.
en.B: So Jesus got back into the boat, crossed the lake, and came to the town where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lived.
en.R: Jesus got into a boat and went back across the lake to the town where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lived.

decisions.choice: his own town: Capernaum
decisions.reason: Jesus had moved to Capernaum (4:13).

decisions.choice: Jesus; the lake
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus and say what he crossed.

source.text: Καὶ ἰδοὺ προσέφερον αὐτῷ παραλυτικὸν ἐπὶ κλίνης βεβλημένον.

records.literal_gloss: And behold, they were bringing to him a paralytic on a bed lying.

en.L: And look, they were bringing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a paralyzed man lying on a bed.
en.B: Some people brought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a paralyzed man lying on a stretcher.
en.R: Some people brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a man who could not walk. He was lying on a mat.

decisions.choice: bed: a light pallet or stretcher on which he was carried
decisions.reason: The word means a bed or couch; one that could be carried is meant, as the man picks it up in 9:6.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

source.text: καὶ ἰδὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν εἶπεν τῷ παραλυτικῷ· Θάρσει, τέκνον· ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι.

records.literal_gloss: And having seen the Jesus the faith of them he said to the paralytic, Take courage, child; are forgiven of you the sins.

en.L: And seeing their faith, Jesus said to the paralyzed man, "Take heart, child; your sins are forgiven."
en.B: Jesus saw their faith and said to the man, "Be encouraged, my son. Your sins are forgiven."
en.R: Jesus saw that they had faith in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He said to the man, "Cheer up, my friend! Your sins are forgiven."

decisions.choice: their faith: the trust of those who brought him, and his own
decisions.reason: "Their" includes the carriers. Their bringing him showed their trust in Jesus.

decisions.choice: are forgiven: God forgives them now, and Jesus declares it
decisions.reason: The present passive speaks of forgiveness given now; the passive points to God. That Jesus speaks it is what offends the scribes (9:3).

decisions.choice: child: an affectionate address
alternatives: a statement of the man's age
decisions.reason: The word means child, used warmly, as an older person might speak to a younger one.

decisions.choice: Be encouraged, my son (B); Cheer up, my friend (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use natural English for a kind address.

source.text: καὶ ἰδού τινες τῶν γραμματέων εἶπαν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Οὗτος βλασφημεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: And behold, some of the scribes said among themselves, This one blasphemes.

en.L: And look, some of the scribes said to themselves, "This [man] blasphemes."
en.B: At this some of the scribes said to themselves, "This man is insulting God!"
en.R: Some of the teachers of the law thought, "This man is speaking as if he were God!"

decisions.choice: blasphemes: insults God by claiming what belongs to God alone
decisions.reason: Only God can forgive sins against him (Isaiah 43:25). To the scribes, Jesus's words claimed God's right.

decisions.choice: is insulting God (B); is speaking as if he were God (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the charge means.

decisions.choice: look (L); at this (B); not rendered (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

source.text: καὶ εἰδὼς ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς ἐνθυμήσεις αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἱνατί ἐνθυμεῖσθε πονηρὰ ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν;

records.literal_gloss: And having known the Jesus the thoughts of them said, Why do you think evil in the hearts of you?

en.L: And Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said, "Why do you think evil in your hearts?
en.B: Jesus knew what they were thinking and said, "Why do you think such evil things in your hearts?
en.R: Jesus knew what they were thinking. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Why are you thinking such evil things?

decisions.choice: knowing their thoughts: Jesus knows what they say only inwardly
decisions.reason: They spoke "to themselves" (9:3). Knowing hearts belongs to God (1 Samuel 16:7; Psalm 139:2).

decisions.choice: evil: wrong and hostile thoughts
decisions.reason: Accusing God's agent of blasphemy is itself wrong in God's sight.

source.text: τί γάρ ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον, εἰπεῖν· Ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι, ἢ εἰπεῖν· Ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει;

records.literal_gloss: Which for is easier, to say, Are forgiven of you the sins, or to say, Get up and walk?

en.L: For which is easier, to say, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?
en.B: Which is easier: to say, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?
en.R: Is it easier to say to this man, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?

decisions.choice: which is easier to say: forgiveness cannot be seen, healing can
decisions.reason: Anyone can say "your sins are forgiven" with no one able to check. A command to walk is tested at once. The healing will show that the unseen word was true.

source.text: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας τότε λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ· Ἐγερθεὶς ἆρόν σου τὴν κλίνην καὶ ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου.

records.literal_gloss: So that but you may know that authority has the Son of the Man on the earth to forgive sins, then he says to the paralytic, Having got up take up of you the bed and go to the house of you.

en.L: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins"—then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to the paralyzed man—"Get up, take up your bed and go to your home."
en.B: But I want you to know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins." Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the paralyzed man, "Get up, pick up your stretcher, and go home."
en.R: I will show you that the Son of Man has the right to forgive sins here on earth." Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the man who could not walk, "Get up, pick up your mat, and go home."

decisions.choice: the sentence breaks off: Jesus turns from the scribes to the man
decisions.reason: Jesus begins a sentence to the scribes and finishes it with action: the command to the paralyzed man.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man has authority on earth: the figure of Daniel 7:13-14
alternatives: any human being has such authority
decisions.reason: In Daniel the one like a son of man receives authority from God. Jesus claims that authority now, on earth, to forgive sins (see 8:20).

decisions.choice: says (L); said (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense.

source.text: καὶ ἐγερθεὶς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And having got up he went away to the house of him.

en.L: And he got up and went away to his home.
en.B: And the man got up and went home.
en.R: And the man got up and went home.

decisions.choice: he got up and went: he does just what he was told
decisions.reason: The words repeat the command of 9:6. The healing is complete and immediate.

source.text: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ ὄχλοι ἐφοβήθησαν καὶ ἐδόξασαν τὸν θεὸν τὸν δόντα ἐξουσίαν τοιαύτην τοῖς ἀνθρώποις.

records.literal_gloss: Having seen then the crowds were afraid and glorified the God the having given authority such to the men.

en.L: And when the crowds saw [it], they were afraid, and they glorified God, who had given such authority to {{gender:human beings|men}}.
en.B: When the crowds saw this, they were filled with awe, and they glorified God for giving such authority to human beings.
en.R: When the people saw this, they were amazed and afraid. They gave glory to God for giving such power to people.

decisions.choice: were afraid: were filled with awe at God's power
decisions.reason: Fear here is the awe people feel before God's work.

decisions.choice: to human beings: to Jesus as a man, and perhaps to those who will act in his name
decisions.reason: The crowds see a man forgive sins. The plural may also look ahead to the authority Jesus gives his followers (16:19; 18:18).

decisions.choice: were afraid, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: marveled, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "marveled". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

source.text: Καὶ παράγων ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκεῖθεν εἶδεν ἄνθρωπον καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον, Μαθθαῖον λεγόμενον, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι· καὶ ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And passing on the Jesus from there saw a man sitting at the tax booth, Matthew called, and he says to him, Follow me; and having got up he followed him.

en.L: And as Jesus passed on from there, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax booth, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to him, "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}." And he got up and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Moving on from there, Jesus noticed a man called Matthew at his seat in the tax office. Jesus said to him, "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}." And Matthew rose and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: As Jesus walked on from there, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw a man named Matthew. Matthew was sitting at the place where he collected taxes. Jesus said to him, "Come, follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}." So Matthew got up and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: the tax booth: where tolls were collected on goods passing through
alternatives: a government office for income tax
decisions.reason: Capernaum lay on a trade route and near the border of Herod Antipas's territory. Toll collectors were despised (5:46).

decisions.choice: Matthew: the tax collector whom Mark and Luke call Levi
decisions.reason: Mark 2:14 and Luke 5:27 tell the same call of "Levi". Matthew 10:3 calls him "Matthew the tax collector". Early Christian tradition named this Matthew as the author of the Gospel; the Gospel itself does not say who wrote it.

decisions.choice: he got up and followed him: an immediate response, leaving his work
decisions.reason: As with the fishermen (4:20, 22), Matthew leaves his trade at once.

decisions.choice: says (L); said (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense.

source.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο αὐτοῦ ἀνακειμένου ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ, καὶ ἰδοὺ πολλοὶ τελῶναι καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἐλθόντες συνανέκειντο τῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And it happened of him reclining in the house, and behold, many tax collectors and sinners having come were reclining with the Jesus and the disciples of him.

en.L: And it happened, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was reclining [at table] in the house, look, many tax collectors and sinners came and were reclining with Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples.
en.B: Then, as Jesus sat at table in the house, a crowd of tax collectors and sinners came and joined {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples for the meal.
en.R: Later Jesus was eating a meal in the house. Many tax collectors and other people known as sinners came and ate with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers.

decisions.choice: the house: probably Matthew's
decisions.reason: Luke 5:29 says Levi gave a feast in his house. Matthew says only "the house".

decisions.choice: sinners: people known for living outside God's law
decisions.reason: The word marked people whose way of life put them outside respectable religious society, such as those in shameful trades.

decisions.choice: reclining with: sharing a meal, a sign of acceptance
alternatives: only being in the same room
decisions.reason: Eating with someone showed fellowship. That is why the Pharisees object (9:11).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

source.text: καὶ ἰδόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἔλεγον τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Διὰ τί μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίει ὁ διδάσκαλος ὑμῶν;

records.literal_gloss: And having seen the Pharisees were saying to the disciples of him, Why with the tax collectors and sinners eats the teacher of you?

en.L: And when the Pharisees saw [this], they said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Why does your teacher eat with the tax collectors and sinners?"
en.B: When the Pharisees saw it, they asked {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?"
en.R: When the Pharisees saw this, they asked {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, "Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?"

decisions.choice: the Pharisees: careful about purity at meals
alternatives: opposed to all meals with others
decisions.reason: The Pharisees kept rules of purity at their tables. Eating with people who did not keep the law would make a teacher unclean in their eyes.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας εἶπεν· Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ἰσχύοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλὰ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες.

records.literal_gloss: He but having heard said, Not need have the being strong of a physician but the badly having.

en.L: But hearing [this], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Those who are strong have no need of a physician, but those who are sick.
en.B: Jesus heard them and said, "People who are well do not need a doctor; sick people do.
en.R: Jesus heard this. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Healthy people do not need a doctor. Sick people do.

decisions.choice: the physician and the sick: Jesus came for those who know they need him
decisions.reason: The proverb pictures Jesus as a doctor and sinners as the sick. It does not say the Pharisees are well; it says why he is with sinners.

source.text: πορευθέντες δὲ μάθετε τί ἐστιν· Ἔλεος θέλω καὶ οὐ θυσίαν· οὐ γὰρ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλούς.

records.literal_gloss: Having gone but learn what is: Mercy I want and not sacrifice; not for I came to call righteous but sinners.

en.L: But go and learn what this means: 'I desire mercy, and not sacrifice.' For I did not come to call [the] righteous, but sinners."
en.B: Go and learn what this saying means: 'I want mercy, not sacrifice.' For I did not come to call righteous people, but sinners."
en.R: Go and find out what this Scripture means: 'I want you to show mercy to people, more than I want you to offer sacrifices.' I did not come to invite good people. I came to invite sinners."

decisions.choice: I desire mercy, not sacrifice: Hosea 6:6
decisions.reason: In Hosea God says he wants faithful love more than offerings. The "not" ranks the two, as Hebrew often does. Jesus quotes it again in 12:7.

decisions.choice: the righteous: those who think they are right with God
alternatives: people who truly have no sin
decisions.reason: There is irony: those who count themselves righteous do not see their need.

decisions.choice: to call: to invite, as to a feast and into the kingdom
decisions.reason: The verb is used of inviting guests (22:3-9).

decisions.choice: more than I want you to offer sacrifices
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the saying ranks mercy above sacrifice.

source.text: Τότε προσέρχονται αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου λέγοντες· Διὰ τί ἡμεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι νηστεύομεν πολλά, οἱ δὲ μαθηταί σου οὐ νηστεύουσιν;

records.literal_gloss: Then come to him the disciples of John saying, Why we and the Pharisees fast often, the but disciples of you not fast?

en.L: Then the disciples of John come to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples do not fast?"
en.B: Next John's disciples came and asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "We fast often, and so do the Pharisees. Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples not fast?"
en.R: Then the followers of John the Baptist came to Jesus. They asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "We and the Pharisees often go without food to pray. Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} followers not do that?"

decisions.choice: we and the Pharisees fast: regular fasting as a mark of devotion
alternatives: the fast of the Day of Atonement only
decisions.reason: Besides the fast the law required, devout groups fasted regularly (6:16; Luke 18:12).

decisions.choice: often, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the word is missing in some early manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts lack "often". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: come (L); came (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ δύνανται οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ νυμφῶνος πενθεῖν ἐφ’ ὅσον μετ’ αὐτῶν ἐστιν ὁ νυμφίος;

records.literal_gloss: And said to them the Jesus, Not can the sons of the bridal chamber mourn as long as with them is the bridegroom?

en.L: And Jesus said to them, "Can the {{gender:guests|sons}} of the bridal chamber mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them?
en.B: Jesus answered, "How can the wedding guests mourn while the bridegroom is with them?
en.R: Jesus said to them, "Friends of a bridegroom do not feel sad while he is with them at the wedding.

decisions.choice: sons of the bridal chamber: the groom's friends and guests at a wedding
decisions.reason: "Sons of" describes those who belong to something. A wedding was a time of feasting, when no one fasted.

decisions.choice: the bridegroom: Jesus, as God is the bridegroom of his people
decisions.reason: In the prophets God is Israel's husband (Isaiah 62:5; Hosea 2:19). Jesus takes that picture for himself, and John's disciples would know the Baptist's words in John 3:29.

decisions.choice: the wedding guests (B); friends of a bridegroom (R)
alternatives: the sons of the bridal chamber
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who is meant. The bridegroom is a figure in a picture, so his pronoun takes no deity_pronoun span, as in John 3:29.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: The question expects "no"; Readable gives the answer.

source.text: ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος, καὶ τότε νηστεύσουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Will come but days when will be taken away from them the bridegroom, and then they will fast.

en.L: But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast.
en.B: But a time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them, and then they will fast.
en.R: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them. Then they will go without food.

decisions.choice: the bridegroom taken away: a hint of Jesus's death
decisions.reason: "Taken away" suggests a violent removal. This is the first hint in Matthew of Jesus's death.

source.text: οὐδεὶς δὲ ἐπιβάλλει ἐπίβλημα ῥάκους ἀγνάφου ἐπὶ ἱματίῳ παλαιῷ· αἴρει γὰρ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἱματίου, καὶ χεῖρον σχίσμα γίνεται.

records.literal_gloss: No one but puts a patch of cloth unshrunk on a garment old; takes away for the fullness of it from the garment, and worse tear happens.

en.L: And no one puts a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; for the patch pulls away from the garment, and a worse tear results.
en.B: No one sews a patch of new, unshrunk cloth onto an old coat. The patch will pull away from the coat, and the tear will be worse.
en.R: No one uses a piece of new cloth to fix a hole in old clothes. The new cloth will shrink and pull away, and the hole will get bigger.

decisions.choice: the new patch and the old garment: what Jesus brings cannot be added to the old ways as a repair
decisions.reason: With the wineskins (9:17), the picture answers the question about fasting. The new time Jesus brings needs new forms.

source.text: οὐδὲ βάλλουσιν οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς· εἰ δὲ μή γε, ῥήγνυνται οἱ ἀσκοί, καὶ ὁ οἶνος ἐκχεῖται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοὶ ἀπόλλυνται· ἀλλὰ βάλλουσιν οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινούς, καὶ ἀμφότεροι συντηροῦνται.

records.literal_gloss: Nor do they put wine new into wineskins old; if but not, burst the wineskins, and the wine is poured out and the wineskins are destroyed; but they put wine new into wineskins fresh, and both are preserved.

en.L: Nor do they put new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wineskins burst, and the wine is poured out and the wineskins are destroyed. But they put new wine into fresh wineskins, and both are preserved."
en.B: And people do not pour new wine into old wineskins. If they do, the skins will split, the wine will run out, and the skins will be ruined. No, they pour new wine into new wineskins, and both are kept safe."
en.R: People do not put new wine into old leather bags. If they do, the bags will break, the wine will spill, and the bags will be ruined. People always put new wine into new bags. Then both the wine and the bags are kept safe."

decisions.choice: wineskins: bags made of goatskin
decisions.reason: New wine was still fermenting and stretched the skin. An old skin, already stretched and dry, would split.

decisions.choice: both are preserved: the new is kept, and nothing is wasted
alternatives: the old is kept as well
decisions.reason: Matthew alone adds these words. They stress that what is new must be given a fitting form so it is not lost.

decisions.choice: leather bags
decisions.reason: Readable describes them.
